Travis Walton joins Joe Rogan to share his gripe with theories about aliens. Walton is the logger whose 1975 tale of being taken by a craft became the film Fire in the Sky. He speaks as a man who says he lived it, not read it.

Walton tells why armchair takes on his case grate on him after all these years. He walks through the night in the woods and the days he was gone, as he recalls them. Rogan asks what he wishes the doubters would grant. Listeners hear a famed witness in his own words. The library holds the segment as an archive record.

Actress Cheryl Hines tells Tucker Carlson how far her life has traveled. She grew up in Orlando and Tallahassee, Florida. One day she drove a small Toyota across the country to Los Angeles.

Hines recalls nearly making that drive alone at the last hour. The title promises stories from her hit comedy Curb Your Enthusiasm. It also covers her support for her husband, Robert F. Kennedy Jr. She discusses fame, family, and political storms. The episode blends warm memoir with a spouse's view of a hard road toward the White House.
podcast-tuckercarlson-djXQCaqT8WQ:
Novelist Walter Kirn updates Tucker Carlson on the case of Luigi Mangione, the accused killer of a health insurance executive. Kirn, author of Up in the Air, has followed the case with a literary eye. He draws strange parallels between Mangione and Lee Harvey Oswald.

Kirn walks through the latest court news and the public's odd fascination with the accused. He compares the scenes, handlers, and questions around both young men and their famous targets. Carlson probes where reporting ends and pattern-hunting begins. Literary and curious viewers get fact meeting fiction in one of the era's strangest cases.

Tucker Carlson opens with a lament for the Britain that once ruled a vast empire. He recalls a nation that held a quarter of the earth's land. Then he turns to guest Piers Morgan.

The title promises a hard test of Morgan's free speech views. Carlson presses him on where speech should stop. Morgan defends lines that Carlson calls weak. The debate ranges over empire, decline, and modern Britain. The episode is a clash of two big media egos, each sure the other fails his own stated test. Neither host gives ground at any point.
